audited_inflection_rules.text: Present1sg -e and plural -að use the present stem; present2/3 require the selected mutation/consonant rules. Preterite1/3sg share the singular stem; preterite2sg uses the plural stem plus -e; all plural persons use -on. Contracted and j-present rows are explicit.
IV normally e/æ/ǣ/o. Learn niman nōm/nōmon and cuman cōm/cōmon separately; cuman present cymst/cymð.
V normally e/æ/ǣ/e. Separate palatal giefan, j-present biddan/licgan/sittan, etan longǣt, and contracted sēon/gesēon. cweðan changes ð to d in plural-based preterite and participle.

VI normally a/ō/ō/a, but j-present and palatal systems require the actual lexical rows. standan loses n in the past; slēan has short ie in present2/3 and g in past; scēop is a checked alternative to scōp.

Cook reduplicating verbs are course classVII: longēo or ē in the preterite, normally same present/participle vowel. wēpan/wōpen and fōn/fangen require explicit rows; hātan active is separate from hātte.
Preserve vowel quantity in umlaut: short ea→ie; longēa→īe; ā→ǣ;ō→ē. Dental combinations and geminate reduction are inherited rules. x plus either -st or -ð gives -xt: weaxan2/3sg both wiext.
biddan/licgan/sittan/hębban/scieppan have explicit consonant patterns; swęrian uses -ie/-est/-eð/-iað present endings like nęrian, but a strong swōr/swōron preterite.
geswīcan/scīnan/flēogan/swimman are new productive lexical systems applying already taught classesI–III. Prior supplied tokens are not prior mastery.
Four principal parts identify stems. Infinitives and participles remain supplied citations with no independent nonfinite recall or syntax; neither passive nor perfect follows from a table.
gesēon and gescieppan are independently evidenced lexemes. Prefix-preserving finite expansion is declared; arbitrary prefix attachment or semantic inference is not taught.

Finite morphology does not determine government. New composed clauses use only the bounded frames in lexical-frames.json and prior taught adjuncts; other selected verbs may be assessed by labelled morphology.

new_compositions.intended_meaning: Two men carried food. Their companions sat in the dwelling. The men gave the companions the food, and they ate. One man did not eat. He gave his food to the birds. The birds ate and flew. The man sat on the shore and saw the fish. The fish swam in the water.

grammar_inventory.description: Complete selected Class IV beran, niman and cuman indicative systems and their principal-part series.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Finite morphology only; each lexical argument frame is separately stated.

grammar_inventory.description: Niman and cuman have their independently selected nasal-family vowel series, including Cook nōm/nōmon and cōm/cōmon and exact present singulars.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Documented alternatives remain valid but do not become assigned extra recall targets.

grammar_inventory.description: Complete selected Class V indicative systems, including the contrast of preterite singular and plural stems.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No nonfinite syntax follows from the four principal parts.

grammar_inventory.description: Cweðan has the checked present2/3 singular changes and ð/d alternation at its exact principal-part positions.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No unrestricted consonant substitution.

grammar_inventory.description: Giefan has its checked palatal present and preterite series, including gēafon.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact selected lexical series, not a universal ge- prefix or spelling rule.

grammar_inventory.description: Biddan, licgan and sittan have j-present geminate patterns, with exact single-consonant present2/3 singulars and their strong pasts.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Present shape alone does not classify the preterite as weak.

grammar_inventory.description: Etan has the exact checked dental present singulars and selected long-vowel singular preterite ǣt.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Accept documented alternatives with their source scope; do not extend quantity changes to unrelated verbs.

grammar_inventory.description: Sēon and separately evidenced gesēon have complete contracted present systems, short ie in singular2/3, and sāw-/gesāw- past plural stems.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: The lemma id geseon is retained; checked display quantity gesēon is an explicit new-system metadata change, not a rewrite of old source transcriptions.

grammar_inventory.description: Complete selected Class VI indicative systems, with the ordinary ō past and each lexical present alternation.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Finite indicative only.

grammar_inventory.description: Slēan has the checked contracted present and selected slōg/slōgon past, retaining short ie in sliehst/sliehð.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Documented slōh-type alternative is separate; no automatic creation of variant tables.

grammar_inventory.description: Standan retains n in the present, loses it in the strong stōd/stōdon past, and has the checked stęntst/stęnt singulars.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Ordinary posture is separate from the earlier locally supplied stand-against construction.

grammar_inventory.description: Hębban, scieppan/gescieppan and swęrian have independently specified j-present subpatterns and strong preterites.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Selected swęrie/swęrest/swęreð/swęriað does not imply that every -ian verb is weak.

grammar_inventory.description: Selected Class VII ēo-past systems share the preterite vowel across singular and plural while retaining distinct present systems and lexical spellings.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: The class name supplies a practical grouping; historical reduplication is not an additional required system.

grammar_inventory.description: Selected Class VII present2/3 singulars have exactly the checked vowel and consonant changes, including weaxan wiext in both persons.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No universal mutation rule is inferred from the class label.

grammar_inventory.description: Lǣtan, hātan and fōn have the selected ē-past systems and their exact present singulars.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Active hātan does not teach anomalous passive hātte, infinitive commands or naming syntax.

grammar_inventory.description: Fōn has its checked contracted present and nasal-stem fēng/fēngon past.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Citation-only fangen does not establish a participial construction.

grammar_inventory.description: Geswīcan, scīnan, flēogan and swimman are new whole finite lexical systems following earlier strong I–III families.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Earlier knowledge of a class, supplied geswāc, and supplied scīnen/scinen are not prior productive mastery of these systems.

grammar_inventory.description: Gesēon, gescieppan and geswīcan are separately evidenced lexical systems with full finite paradigms and their stated senses.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No productive prefix attachment or automatic aspect/sense rule.

grammar_inventory.description: Beran in carry and niman in take have an accusative person/thing as their selected ordinary object.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: The new food/fish examples are declared ordinary lexical applications, not falsely attributed source quotations; no goal or source preposition is introduced.

grammar_inventory.description: Giefan gives an accusative thing to a dative recipient, with prior noun, pronoun and possessive forms.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Companions and birds as recipients are declared ordinary applications; no new benefactive or clausal construction.

grammar_inventory.description: Sittan, licgan and standan describe ordinary intransitive posture; a previously taught locative on+dative phrase may locate the subject.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No causal placement, directional complement or stand-against construction is inferred.

grammar_inventory.description: Etan means eat, with an accusative food object or with the food understood in an ordinary objectless use.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No partitive genitive, infinitive complement or idiom of consuming something figuratively is assigned.

grammar_inventory.description: Sēon and gesēon take an accusative person/thing in the selected ordinary see use.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Their source content clauses remain supplied; no infinitive-of-perception or general complement rule.

grammar_inventory.description: Feallan is used intransitively for falling.

grammar_inventory.description: Flēogan fly, scīnan shine, swimman swim and weaxan grow have their independently checked ordinary intransitive uses.

grammar_inventory.description: Slēan strike and healdan hold take an accusative person/thing in their selected ordinary physical senses.
